fixes.issue: substitute_strategy_holes (lib.rs:327-346) raw str::replace over ascending BTreeMap: ?WG corrupts ?WG2 -> shared[i32,1282] (empirically proven silent miscompile). Third naive-text-transform instance (M3.14, M3.15).
fixes.resolution: Boundary-safe substitution. Exact mechanism = a single left-to-right manual scan (regex-free): at each '?', greedily match the LONGEST hole name present at that offset whose FOLLOWING byte is NOT [A-Za-z0-9_], substitute and advance; else copy the byte. The following-byte boundary check is the SOUND guarantee; longest-name-first is only a same-offset tiebreak, not relied on alone. Single forward scan also eliminates the ascending-order hazard. Protects all callers incl. rewrite-verify's compile_source_with_assignments. Defense-in-depth: union_module_holes ALSO fails closed EnumerateError::PrefixCollidingHoleNames{shorter,longer} at discovery time (~10 LOC). Both layers ship.
fixes.comment_scope_decision: The boundary fix is prefix-safe but DELIBERATELY NOT comment-aware. Raw substitution already rewrites ?name inside // comments today (pre-existing; substitute path is not lexer-anchored). A substituted comment is semantically HARMLESS — the lexer discards comments before HIR, so it cannot change compiled SPIR-V, hole resolution, or golden bytes. The miscompile the fix closes lives only in LIVE code. So comment-awareness of the SUBSTITUTE path is deferred with rationale; this is CORRECT asymmetry vs the STRIP path (which IS lexer-anchored, because there a comment decoy removes the WRONG block — a real failure mode). AT-2968(b) pins a `// ?WG2` comment-decoy: the LIVE ?WG2 still resolves to 64, resolved source has no 1282.
fixes.spec_note_added: Project-wide durable note in §4: 3rd naive-text-transform footgun (M3.14/M3.15/M3.21); any future text transform on ?holes/@annotations/identifiers MUST be token/boundary-disciplined; a bare .replace("?"..)/.find("@"..) on live source is a defect on sight.
